oracle_clues: Repro explicitly checks for the exception message `SVD did not converge` for NaN input.
Repro also shows the NumPy warning `RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in det` from `numpy/linalg/_linalg.py:2406`.

category_specific_evidence: The failure/warning involved NaN values: “invalid value encountered in det” followed by “Exception caught for NaN values: SVD did not converge” (issue#26413).
The algorithmic issue is in `Rotation.from_matrix()` orthonormalization for “arbitrary user inputs” rather than matrices already near orthonormal.

The existing algorithm works only for matrices “already near orthonormal” and was “designed to correct for round-off error,” while the SVD-based method aims to correctly solve the orthogonal Procrustes problem.

The PR text provides an example claim: the existing example in the docs shows an “extremely poor result which is 22.6 degrees (!!) off the exact solution,” and left-handed matrices “return even worse results” (PR#22418 / pr_body).

A test ensures right-handed rotation matrices by checking `dets = np.linalg.det(mat)` and flipping the matrix if `dets[i] < 0` before calling `Rotation.from_matrix(mat).as_matrix()` (test_rotation.py).
The reported repro matrix in issue#22417 uses entries with magnitudes like 0.5 and 0.0, e.g. a 3x3 matrix with values [[0, -0.5, 0],[0.5, 0, 0],[0, 0, 0.5]].
The repro for issue#22417 compares “Exact SVD method” output `U @ Vt` against “Inaccurate existing method” output from `R.from_matrix(a).as_matrix()` (issue#22417).
reproduction_risks: Evidence does not specify dtype/precision; reproduction may differ depending on float precision (evidence silent).
Evidence does not specify magnitude regime beyond “arbitrary user inputs” vs “already near orthonormal,” and no numeric magnitude thresholds are given (evidence silent).
Evidence does not specify any numerical tolerance used to distinguish correct vs incorrect results (evidence silent).

Handling NaNs is implicated by issue#26413 (“invalid value encountered in det” and “SVD did not converge”), so reproductions using inputs that generate NaNs may fail differently than pure accuracy discrepancies (evidence limited to that warning/exception).

Left-handed vs right-handed matrices are explicitly disallowed/handled; reproduction inputs must consider determinant sign (test shows flipping when det < 0) and the PR text states left-handed matrices behave worse (PR#22418).
